storyboard.addedInformation: The shield says the halt protects the project; the narration only says they halt it.
storyboard.claim: The Blue colleague halting the project over an appendix error is a safeguard, not sabotage.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A Blue office worker holding up a project file beside a large shield guarding it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the Blue-as-brakes idea: the cold logic the team needs.

storyboard.addedInformation: Magnifier in hand shows precision as a need, not nitpicking; stages the negation as a drive.
storyboard.claim: They are not a pedantic idiot; they run on a need for precision.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Office worker closely inspecting a page with a magnifier, focused, not mocking.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Reframes the halt from beat 160 as an untranslated Blue need.

storyboard.addedInformation: The grid makes the map literal: four baselines when calm before stress hits.
storyboard.claim: We now have the map of the four baselines when calm.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The Four-Color Grid matrix of Red Yellow Green Blue presented as the finished map.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Pulls back from Blue detail to the whole four-color system.

storyboard.addedInformation: Fire makes the stress test physical: calm dinner party versus burning building.
storyboard.claim: The real test is behavior under stress, when the building is on fire.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A small office building icon with flames rising from it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns from the calm map to the stress test that breaks it.

storyboard.addedInformation: The held mask slipping off the face shows the public face failing at 3 p.m.
storyboard.claim: Under stress the masks slip; the crucible is Tuesday at 3 p.m.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Two opposite types coming apart under the same stress — the mask slipping is the behaviour changing, not a literal mask.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the mechanism for the fire: the public face comes off.

storyboard.addedInformation: The walking head entering the open plan stages the announcement as an intrusion.
storyboard.claim: The department head walks into the open plan office to announce the deadline.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A manager striding into an open plan office of desks while workers look up.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Drops into the staged crucible: time, place, announcement.

storyboard.addedInformation: The clock shows next-month time collapsing; the client move is a time shock.
storyboard.claim: The next-month deadline is suddenly moved up by the client.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A wall clock beside a calendar page flipping from next month to now.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Delivers the blow announced in beat 165: the date moves.

storyboard.addedInformation: The Red leaping up and jabbing at the desk stages cortisol as aggression.
storyboard.claim: Now due Friday: total crisis, and the Red explodes up slamming the desk.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A heavy older boss in a suit standing over a desk, palm striking it, jaw set.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the moved date to the body's reaction: the Red detonates.

storyboard.addedInformation: The jabbing finger at the team stages blame as a shouted hunt, not a question.
storyboard.claim: The Red screams who messed up the timeline and the contract.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The Red boss jabbing a finger across the desk, shouting at the team.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the Red outburst: slam becomes shouted accusation.

storyboard.addedInformation: The crosshair says the rage is targeted hunting, then pivots to ask about Blue.
storyboard.claim: Enraged, the Red hunts a scapegoat to sacrifice.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A targeting reticle fixed on one fleeing team member while the Red boss points.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Labels the scream from beat 168 as scapegoat hunting.

storyboard.addedInformation: Crossed arms and leaned-back sit stage the shutdown as withdrawal, not work.
storyboard.claim: The Blue shuts down momentum, declaring Friday mathematically impossible.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An office worker leaned back in an ergonomic chair, arms crossed, flat face.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Cuts from Red attack to the opposite pole: Blue freeze.

storyboard.addedInformation: The held spec sheet with its old email trail shows precision clinging to paper.
storyboard.claim: The Blue cites a three-week-old email and a page-four typo.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A worker holding up a marked spec sheet and email printout, pointing at one line.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the Blue freeze its evidence: the documented typo.

storyboard.addedInformation: weak: chaos itself has no literal icon; the strained thinker carries pressure without adapting.
storyboard.claim: Under immense pressure people do not adapt.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An office worker gripping their head at a chaotic desk, papers askew, frozen mid-thought.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Pulls back from Red and Blue to the mechanism: pure chaos, no adaptation.

storyboard.addedInformation: The hunched digging-in posture shows regression to deepest habits, not growth.
storyboard.claim: Maxed-out people dig in and regress to deepest habits.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A worker hunched over a desk, shoulders dug in, refusing new papers pushed toward them.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Extends the no-adaptation claim: overload means regression.

storyboard.addedInformation: The grotesque oversized mask shows traits swelling into caricature.
storyboard.claim: Natural traits distort into exaggerated caricatures.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An oversized grinning grimace-mask beside the explainer, knobs torn loose.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Visualizes digging in as distortion: the knobs rip off.

storyboard.addedInformation: The usually laughing Yellow slumped silent shows charm collapsing with structure.
storyboard.claim: The charming fluid Yellow feels the structure collapse.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The blonde storyteller slumped at a meeting table, charm gone, hands fallen still.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns to the Yellow seat in the same crisis room.

storyboard.addedInformation: Thrown-up hands and open wail stage sulk and joke-deflect as loud complaint.
storyboard.claim: The Yellow turns sulky, deflecting with jokes and complaints about negativity.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The same woman throwing her hands in the air, loudly complaining at glum colleagues.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the Yellow collapse: sulk becomes loud deflection.

storyboard.addedInformation: The blank monitor stare stages vag-nerve apathy as visible shutdown.
storyboard.claim: The Green freezes, staring blankly at the monitor, fully apathetic.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An office worker staring blankly at a glowing monitor, hands dead in lap.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Cuts from Yellow noise to Green silence: the freeze pole.

storyboard.addedInformation: The cowering slump shows terror of a catastrophic mistake choosing paralysis.
storyboard.claim: Terrified of a catastrophic mistake, the Green chooses to do nothing.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A worker hunched low over a keyboard, hands pulled back, afraid to touch anything.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the freeze: fear picks vanishing over error.

storyboard.addedInformation: The manager slumped between empty chairs shows invisibility as a leadership nightmare.
storyboard.claim: The Green goes invisible, hoping conflict evaporates: a manager's nightmare.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A manager gesturing at empty chairs where the team has melted away.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From Green vanishing to the manager left holding the crisis.

storyboard.addedInformation: The four buckets sort the chaos from beats 167-179 into one legible map.
storyboard.claim: The team splits four ways: Red attacks, Blue stalls, Yellow whines, Green paralyzed.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Four labeled buckets sorting the four crisis reactions side by side.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Summarizes the whole crucible scene as four opposite reactions.

storyboard.addedInformation: The juggling-thinker pose stages leading four psychologies as overload.
storyboard.claim: Leading four opposite stress reactions feels like impossible babysitting.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A manager rubbing their temple, juggling four colored balls labeled by reaction.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the four-way split into the leader's question: how do I lead this.

storyboard.addedInformation: The raised blocking hand shows one cure cannot fit all; it would harm half.
storyboard.claim: No universal antidote works for stress relief.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The explainer holding up one hand to stop, blocking a single cure-all bottle.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Answers the juggling question with the paradox: one cure fails.

storyboard.addedInformation: The Red shoving away a soft approach shows calming sameness traumatizing him.
storyboard.claim: Calming everyone the same way traumatizes half; you cannot cuddle a Red.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The Red boss shoving away a comforting hand, glaring, demanding space.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Applies the paradox: soft calming backfires on Red.

storyboard.addedInformation: The struck target shows friction restored as control: a win to burn off rage.
storyboard.claim: A Red needs a tangible obstacle to smash, a micro battle to regain control.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The Red boss smashing a fist through a small target board, triumphant and focused.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the Red cure after the failed cuddle: push, don't soothe.

storyboard.addedInformation: The explainer pivoting between Red and Green warns the same friction flips meaning.
storyboard.claim: Fuel Reds with friction to conquer, but that same tactic breaks a Green.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The explainer gesturing from a charging Red toward a shrinking Green colleague.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Pivots the Red cure toward its danger: never use it on Green.

storyboard.addedInformation: The dragged-to-center worker crumpling shows hard pressure producing tears.
storyboard.claim: Push a stressed Green hard or drag them center stage and they cry.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A Green worker dragged to the middle of the room, head bowed, tears welling.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows what Red friction does to Green: public pressure breaks them.

storyboard.addedInformation: The lone figure curled in a quiet corner shows retreat costing a month of work.
storyboard.claim: Shattered, the Green retreats deep into a shell for a month.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A lone worker curled in a quiet corner room, turned away from the office door.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Extends the tears into long withdrawal: pressure removed too late.

storyboard.addedInformation: The shield over the quiet desk shows safety, not pressure, relieving Green stress.
storyboard.claim: Relieve Green stress with a quiet task and reassurance they belong.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A calm worker at a small quiet desk under a sheltering shield, breathing easy.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the Green cure after the Red cure: remove pressure, grant safety.

storyboard.addedInformation: The shouting worker shows crisis idiocy as pain speaking its mother tongue.
storyboard.claim: Crisis idiocy is not incompetence but a stress response screaming for help.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An anguished worker shouting across the office, hands clutching their head.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Reframes the whole crucible: idiocy was cognitive pain.

storyboard.addedInformation: The pulled-off-shelf dictionary makes translation a physical book choice.
storyboard.claim: Your job is rapid translation: pick the right dictionary by fast observation.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The explainer pulling one dictionary off a shelf of four colored phrasebooks.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns pain into task: translate fast by observing.

storyboard.addedInformation: The rejected long test form shows real typing needs no 40-question sit-down.
storyboard.claim: You type people without a 40-question psychometric test before hello.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A worker pushing away a thick 40-question test form, hands raised in refusal.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Questions the method: how to translate without a formal test.

storyboard.addedInformation: The striding legs in a public plaza show gait itself as the diagnostic.
storyboard.claim: Watch behavior kinematics: how they walk across public space.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Three walkers crossing a plaza with very different strides while one watches.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Answers the test question: observe movement, not paperwork.

storyboard.addedInformation: The espresso cup and square view set the observation post for the next four types.
storyboard.claim: Sit at a sidewalk cafe with an espresso overlooking a crowded square.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A watcher seated at a small cafe table with an espresso, square spreading beyond.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Sets the scene for the walking experiment: the cafe lookout.

storyboard.addedInformation: The arrow-straight charge through the crowd stages Red as velocity.
storyboard.claim: First, the Red: brisk, aggressive, perfectly straight.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The heavy suited boss striding arrow-straight through the square crowd.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: First walker enters the square watched from the cafe.

storyboard.addedInformation: The locked horizon gaze shows no dodging: others must move.
storyboard.claim: No detours: gaze locked on the horizon, dodging no one.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The same strider eyes fixed ahead, cutting straight while others sidestep.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the Red walk: straight line means no yielding.

storyboard.addedInformation: The parting onlookers show forceful intent dominating the pavement.
storyboard.claim: The crowd parts: forceful intent physically dominates the pavement.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The Red powering through the square while the crowd physically steps aside to clear a lane for him.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Completes the Red pass: the crowd yields to intent.

storyboard.addedInformation: The zigzag weaving path contrasts the straight Red line.
storyboard.claim: Then the Yellow: a meandering chaotic path, hugging a neighbor.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The laughing blonde woman weaving across the square to hug a passerby.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Second walker contrasts the first: Red line versus Yellow wander.

storyboard.addedInformation: Shoulder pats and close leaning show tactile warmth invading every bubble.
storyboard.claim: The Yellow pats vendors, chats dog walkers, highly tactile.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The same woman patting a vendor's shoulder and leaning close to a dog walker.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the Yellow wander: hugs become pats and close chats.

storyboard.addedInformation: The still edge-stander shows Blue typing as motionless system-watch.
storyboard.claim: Now the Blue: perfectly still at the square's edge, observing the system.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A motionless office worker at the square's edge, arms still, scanning the crowd.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Third walker contrasts both: noise and force versus still watch.
